The roiling orange corona of a nearby sun dominates the frame, colossal magnetic arcs of plasma looping thousands of kilometers high, the surface a seething granular texture of white-gold, deep amber, and scalding crimson, raw solar wind hazing the edges.

A star-dense galactic core blazes overhead, the bright central bulge a smear of ivory and gold packing millions of suns, dark dust lanes threading through, the outer arms spiraling into blue-violet haze, the whole structure curving impossibly vast.

A cratered grey moon surface slides past below, its terminator casting long black shadows across basin rims and ancient impact scars, a sliver of distant blue planet hanging at the top corner of frame, star-field above utterly dense.

An ice-blue ocean world fills the lower two-thirds, enormous ivory spiral storms coiling across its face, sunlight glinting off polar ice caps, wispy cloud bands streaking east across deep cobalt ocean unbroken by any continent.

A blood-red dying star sits bloated on the frame's horizon, its swollen envelope of expelled gas forming concentric amber and crimson shells around it, a planetary nebula halo shimmering pale violet beyond, surrounding stars tinged ruddy in its ancient light.

A distant blue marble hangs centred in pure black, the Milky Way arching behind it in a dense river of silver and gold starlight, the galaxy's core glowing amber at the peak of the arch, the planet impossibly small and alone.

Twin gas giants hang side by side, one amber-banded and enormous, one smaller and electric-teal, their gravitational tidal bulges visibly distorting each atmosphere, a shared debris ring looping between them catching backlit sunlight in a shimmering golden arc.

A vast emission nebula fills the entire frame, deep crimson hydrogen clouds billowing like thunderheads, pierced by columns of dark molecular dust, newborn O-type stars burning electric-blue at their tips, the whole structure backlit by a hidden stellar nursery.

A rogue comet blazes across the upper frame, its nucleus a jagged grey-white boulder trailing twin tails — one blue ion tail streaming straight, one curved amber dust tail sweeping wide — with a dense starfield and faint galactic haze behind.

The terminator of a volcanic moon cuts diagonally across the frame, its dark side erupting with dozens of glowing orange lava calderas visible from orbit, sulphur-yellow plains catching the sun's rim, Jupiter-like parent planet rising colossal in the background.

A dense globular cluster dominates the backdrop, half a million ancient yellow and orange stars packed into a blazing sphere that grades from blinding white core to scattered outliers, surrounding space a rich cobalt-black dusted with background galaxies.

A supernova remnant expands across the frame, gossamer filaments of shock-heated gas glowing in electric teal, magenta, and amber, the blast wave visible as a translucent bubble-edge crossing the star field, a faint neutron star pinprick at its centre.

A binary star system blazes in the background, a blue-white primary and a smaller golden companion locked in tight orbit, a swirling accretion disk of superheated plasma connecting them in a luminous amber-white bridge, surrounding stars smeared by heat-shimmer haze.

A deep rift valley canyon system on a rust-red world stretches across the lower frame, layered cliff walls kilometres high catching slanted sunlight, a thin wispy atmosphere haze hugging the surface, two small moons mid-transit visible in the salmon-pink sky.

A protoplanetary disk surrounds a young orange star filling the frame, concentric rings of dust and rock debris in ochre, cream, and grey, gaps carved by forming planets, the star itself partially veiled by infalling gas and glinting through curtains of dust.

A magnetar's warped spacetime neighbourhood pulses in the backdrop, concentric rings of X-ray glow layering out from a tiny star-dense point, bending background starlight into arcing Einstein-ring halos, the whole region shimmering with ghostly blue-white gravitational lensing distortions.

A moon-sized asteroid tumbles slowly in the frame's centre, its surface a mosaic of silver-grey regolith, black carbon patches, and bright olivine streaks, craters of all sizes overlapping, the Milky Way's full width spread magnificently behind in silver and gold.

A ringed ice-giant, deep cobalt and teal-banded, hangs at a severe tilt, its rings nearly edge-on but catching backlit sunlight as a thin gold-white slash, a small shepherd moon visibly warping one ring edge, storm hexagons faint at the poles.

A galactic collision fills the frame, two spiral galaxies overlapping, their arms pulled into tidal bridges of white and gold starlight, millions of new blue stars igniting in the overlap zone, dark dust lanes from both systems tangling in long curves.

A bright quasar blasts a relativistic jet directly toward the viewer, the jet a blinding blue-white spear of synchrotron radiation, the host galaxy a smeared ellipse of gold around the blazing core, surrounding space alive with lensed ghost-arc images.

The curved limb of an enormous ringed gas giant fills the top half, its rings casting crisp parallel shadow-bands onto the upper atmosphere below, the night side glowing with deep auroral curtains of green and violet at both poles.

A star-forming region dense with pink and amber Bok globules fills the frame, each dark globule silhouetted against glowing ionised hydrogen clouds, hot young blue stars punching holes of cleared space, bright reflection nebulae pooling electric-blue around the brightest sources.

A tidally locked desert world hangs edge-on to its red-dwarf star, the day side a scorched orange-white half, the night side absolute black, the terminator a sliver of red-lit rock smeared with a thin atmospheric glow of pale violet haze.

A dense dark nebula — a vast coal-black interstellar cloud — blots half the frame, its silhouette ragged and sculptural against a brilliant star-field behind, its edges backlit red and amber where embedded stars heat the dust, a few embedded stars glowing through.

A shattered moon surrounds its parent planet in a gleaming debris ring, fragments ranging from house-sized boulders to dust, backlit into a luminous amber halo, the banded gas giant beneath reflecting gold across the fresh rubble field in a cascade of warm light.
